name: Event-Driven Operations
description: Implement reactive automation using event rulebooks and decision environments to enable self-healing infrastructure operations with reduced MTTR.
authors: Red Hat Ansible Foundations Practice Team

narratives.name: Transforming Manual Incident Response into Self-Healing Infrastructure Operations
narratives.description: How event-driven automation transforms reactive manual operations into proactive self-healing infrastructure management.

narrativeContexts.context: Organizations managing infrastructure at scale face constant alerts from monitoring systems, requiring operations teams to manually assess each incident, determine the appropriate remediation playbook, and execute corrective actions -- a process measured in minutes to hours that does not scale.

The operations team must connect infrastructure event streams to automation decisions, author conditional rulebooks that match event patterns to remediation actions, and build custom decision environments packaging specialized event source plugins -- progressively moving from simple webhook triggers to sophisticated stateful event correlation.

Event-Driven Ansible integrates monitoring systems, message queues, and cloud provider event buses through EDA controller rulebook activations that continuously process events using the Drools decision framework, with in-flight event persistence ensuring no events are lost during controller restarts, while custom decision environments package the specific plugins and dependencies required for each event domain.

Self-healing operations auto-remediate common incident patterns with documented success rates exceeding eighty percent, escalation rules trigger human intervention only for complex or novel events, and post-incident reports are generated automatically -- reducing MTTR from hours to seconds while freeing operations teams to focus on strategic reliability improvements.

narratives.name: Managed Infrastructure as EDA Remediation Targets
narratives.description: How event-driven automation acts on managed infrastructure assets to achieve self-healing operations.

narrativeContexts.context: Managed infrastructure assets -- servers, VMs, containers, network devices, cloud resources -- generate continuous streams of monitoring events indicating health, performance, and compliance status.

When these assets experience failures, performance degradation, or configuration drift, operations teams must manually interpret alerts and execute remediation playbooks, creating response delays that scale linearly with the number of managed assets.

Event-Driven Ansible connects managed asset monitoring to automated remediation through rulebook activations that match event patterns to corrective actions, transforming managed assets from passive monitoring targets into actively self-healing infrastructure components.

narratives.name: Building Intelligent Event Automation from Simple Triggers to Correlated Responses
narratives.description: How event rulebooks progress from basic event matching to sophisticated stateful correlation with optimized routing.

narrativeContexts.context: Infrastructure monitoring systems generate thousands of events daily across compute, network, storage, and application domains, each requiring assessment and potential corrective action that operations teams cannot address at scale through manual processes.

The operations team must author YAML rulebooks defining event sources, conditional rules using the Drools framework, and automated actions that progressively evolve from simple webhook triggers to multi-condition logic, stateful event correlation, and optimized event routing across specialized activations.

Rulebook development begins with basic event matching against single sources, advances to multi-condition logic extracting event attributes as variables with severity-based action branching, then implements stateful correlation tracking event sequences over time windows with threshold-based triggers and event suppression, and finally optimizes routing across multiple specialized activations with event enrichment and chaining via post_event.

Mature event rulebooks reduce mean time to remediation from hours to seconds for common incident patterns, with correlation logic preventing alert storms from triggering duplicate actions and routing ensuring each event domain is handled by specialized, purpose-built rulebook activations.

narratives.name: Purpose-Built Python Runtimes for Event Processing at Scale
narratives.description: How decision environments evolve from default containers to governed catalogs of validated, purpose-built runtimes.

narrativeContexts.context: Event-Driven Ansible requires container runtimes -- decision environments -- that package ansible-core with the specific event source plugins and Python dependencies needed for each event processing domain.

The default decision environment supports only common event sources, and organizations integrating specialized monitoring systems or cloud provider event buses must build and maintain their own decision environment images with appropriate plugins, certificates, and dependency chains.

Organizations establish a governed catalog of purpose-built decision environments -- each validated for performance, scanned for security vulnerabilities, and maintained with automated rebuild pipelines -- ensuring every rulebook activation has access to a reliable, approved runtime tailored to its specific event processing requirements.

narratives.name: Evolving Rulebook Definitions from Simple Triggers to Production-Hardened Logic
narratives.description: How rulebook definition artifacts mature from basic event matching to production-grade stateful correlation with error handling.

narrativeContexts.context: Operations teams need codified event-to-action mappings that translate infrastructure monitoring signals into automated remediation workflows.
Develop YAML rulebook definitions that progressively incorporate multi-condition logic, stateful event correlation, and production hardening with error handling and versioned rollback capability.

Begin with single-source basic rules, add AND/OR logic with severity-based branching and variable extraction, implement stateful correlation with time windows and threshold triggers using group_by_attributes, and harden with error handling, performance optimization, and automated testing suites.
Production-hardened rulebook definitions deliver reliable automated remediation at scale with documented behavior, synthetic test validation, and versioned rollback capability.

narratives.name: Container Runtime Specifications for Reliable Event Processing
narratives.description: How decision environment definitions mature from default specifications to governed catalog entries with security scanning.

narrativeContexts.context: EDA controller requires container runtimes specified through definition files that declare event source plugin dependencies, Python packages, and enterprise certificates.

Default decision environments support only common event sources, and organizations integrating specialized monitoring infrastructure must maintain custom DE specifications with appropriate build pipelines and security validation.

Organizations establish governed DE catalog entries with security scanning, performance validation, lifecycle policies, and automated rebuild pipelines ensuring every rulebook activation references an approved, up-to-date container runtime.

activities.name: Scope Event-Driven Automation Requirements
activities.description: Evaluate infrastructure event streams and define event-driven automation requirements.

narratives.name: Identifying Event-Driven Automation Opportunities Across Infrastructure Domains
narratives.description: How to evaluate infrastructure monitoring systems and identify candidates for event-driven automation.

narrativeContexts.context: Operations teams face a growing volume of infrastructure alerts that require manual assessment and remediation, and must determine which event categories and infrastructure domains are candidates for automated event-driven responses.

Evaluate existing monitoring systems and alert categories across compute, network, storage, security, and application domains to identify event sources suitable for EDA integration, assess event volume and latency requirements, and determine whether default or custom decision environments are needed.

Catalog existing monitoring systems and their event output formats, map alert categories to potential automated remediation actions, quantify event volume and response latency requirements, and assess the default decision environment capabilities against specialized plugin needs for each event source type.

Documented event-driven automation requirements including prioritized event source integrations, identified decision environment customization needs, and a phased implementation roadmap starting with low-risk, high-value event categories.

activities.name: Configure Event Source Integrations
activities.description: Integrate infrastructure event streams with EDA controller for reactive automation.

narratives.name: Connecting Infrastructure Monitoring to Automated Event Processing
narratives.description: How to select, configure, and validate event source integrations from monitoring systems to EDA controller.

narrativeContexts.context: Infrastructure monitoring systems -- Prometheus Alertmanager, Datadog, Splunk, cloud provider event buses, and message queues -- generate continuous streams of alerts that must be connected to the EDA controller for automated processing.
Select and configure event source integrations matching infrastructure telemetry systems, implementing appropriate authentication, network isolation, and payload transformation for each source type.

Configure webhook event sources with TLS termination and authentication, set up Kafka consumers with SASL authentication and consumer group settings, subscribe to cloud provider event buses with appropriate IAM permissions, and establish pull-based sources for polling-based monitoring, validating event delivery with controlled injection testing.

Infrastructure event streams reliably deliver monitoring data to EDA controller rulebook activations with validated authentication, network isolation, and rate limiting preventing unauthorized access and event flooding.

activities.name: Author Event Automation Rulebooks
activities.description: Create conditional automation logic mapping infrastructure events to remediation actions.

narratives.name: Authoring Conditional Event-to-Action Mappings with Multi-Condition Logic
narratives.description: How to author YAML rulebooks with conditional logic, severity-based branching, and variable extraction.

narrativeContexts.context: Connected event sources deliver infrastructure alerts to the EDA controller, but these events require conditional logic that maps different event types, severities, and contexts to appropriate remediation actions with variable extraction and priority ordering.

Author YAML rulebooks defining event sources, conditional rules using the Drools framework with AND/OR logic, severity-based action branching, extra_vars extraction, and rule priority ordering to ensure correct execution sequences.

Define rulebook structure with sources and rules sections, implement condition matching using dot notation for nested event attributes with boolean operators, configure actions with variable substitution passing event context, test locally using ansible-rulebook CLI against synthetic event payloads, and deploy to EDA controller as rulebook activations.

Rulebooks with multi-condition logic reliably match diverse event patterns and trigger appropriate remediation actions with full event context passed to downstream automation workflows through extra_vars.

activities.name: Provision Default Decision Environment
activities.description: Deploy default Red Hat decision environment for basic event processing capability.

narratives.name: Establishing Baseline Event Processing Runtime Capability
narratives.description: How to deploy and validate the default decision environment for initial event processing.

narrativeContexts.context: EDA controller requires a decision environment container runtime to execute rulebook activations, and Red Hat provides a default DE supporting common event sources including webhook, Kafka, and AWS events.

The default DE must be properly deployed and validated before teams can begin developing rulebook activations, and its limitations for specialized event sources must be documented to inform custom DE planning.

Deploy the default decision environment to EDA controller, validate it supports the initial target event sources, document its capabilities and limitations, and configure it as the baseline runtime for initial rulebook activation development.

activities.name: Build Custom Decision Environments
activities.description: Create custom decision environment container images with specialized event source plugins.

narratives.name: Packaging Specialized Event Source Plugins into Custom Container Runtimes
narratives.description: How to build custom decision environment container images for specialized event processing domains.

narrativeContexts.context: Organizations integrating specialized monitoring systems, cloud provider event buses, or custom event sources discover that the default decision environment lacks the specific plugins and Python dependencies required for their event processing domains.
Build custom decision environment container images that package the necessary event source plugins, Python dependencies, and enterprise TLS certificates required by each event processing domain.

Create DE definition files specifying event source plugins and dependencies, build container images using Dockerfile or ansible-builder, include custom CA certificates for enterprise TLS requirements, publish custom DEs to container registry accessible by EDA controller, and validate rulebook activations reference the correct custom DE.

Custom decision environments provide specialized runtimes for each event processing domain with validated plugin dependencies, enterprise TLS certificates, and reproducible builds published to container registry.

activities.name: Implement Stateful Event Correlation
activities.description: Develop stateful rulebooks correlating related events over time windows.

narratives.name: Correlating Multi-Source Events for Intelligent Remediation Decisions
narratives.description: How to implement stateful event correlation using throttle and multiple-event patterns.

narrativeContexts.context: Simple event-to-action mappings trigger remediation for individual events, but infrastructure incidents often manifest as cascading alerts across multiple sources that require correlated analysis to determine root cause and appropriate response.

Implement stateful event correlation using throttle and multiple-event patterns that track event sequences over configurable time windows, applying threshold-based triggers and suppressing duplicate remediation actions.

Implement throttle mechanisms using group_by_attributes to aggregate events from the same source with once_within suppression windows, develop multi-event correlation using all/any conditions with time-bounded windows, preserve accumulated context passing correlated data to downstream remediation actions, and document correlation patterns with real-world incident examples.

Stateful event correlation prevents alert storm cascades from triggering duplicate remediation actions, identifies genuine incident patterns requiring automated response, and provides accumulated context to downstream remediation playbooks enabling more targeted corrective actions.

activities.name: Deploy Rulebook Activations for Managed Assets
activities.description: Deploy and operate rulebook activations targeting managed infrastructure for automated remediation.

narratives.name: Operating Event-Driven Remediation Across Managed Infrastructure Assets
narratives.description: How to deploy production rulebook activations for continuous managed asset monitoring and remediation.

narrativeContexts.context: Managed infrastructure assets -- servers, VMs, containers, network devices, and cloud resources -- generate operational events indicating health issues, performance degradation, or configuration drift that require automated corrective action.

Deploy production rulebook activations that continuously monitor managed asset events, route events to appropriate specialized activations by infrastructure domain, and execute remediation playbooks targeting affected assets with verification steps confirming successful resolution.

Deploy rulebook activations to EDA controller configured for managed asset monitoring domains, implement event routing partitioning event streams by asset category and severity, activate in-flight event persistence ensuring no events are lost during controller maintenance, and configure remediation verification steps that validate affected assets have returned to healthy state.

Managed infrastructure assets receive continuous automated monitoring and remediation through rulebook activations, with event routing ensuring each infrastructure domain is handled by specialized activations and in-flight persistence guaranteeing reliable event processing during controller maintenance windows.

activities.name: Validate Decision Environment Performance
activities.description: Test and optimize decision environment performance under production event volumes.

narratives.name: Validating Event Processing Runtime Capacity Under Production Load
narratives.description: How to validate decision environment performance and establish resource profiles.

narrativeContexts.context: Custom decision environments are deployed to EDA controller handling production event streams, and their performance characteristics determine the overall reliability and latency of event-driven automation.

Without systematic load testing and resource profiling, decision environments may fail under production event volumes, exhibit memory leaks during long-running activations, or introduce unacceptable latency between event receipt and action execution.

Validate each decision environment with load testing simulating expected event volumes, profile memory and CPU utilization to identify optimization opportunities, document resource requirements and capacity limits, and establish versioning with rollback procedures enabling rapid recovery from problematic DE deployments.

activities.name: Implement Self-Healing Event Remediation
activities.description: Establish autonomous event-driven remediation with escalation rules and post-incident reporting.

narratives.name: Achieving Autonomous Infrastructure Remediation Within Governed Boundaries
narratives.description: How to establish self-healing operations with escalation rules and automated post-incident reporting.

narrativeContexts.context: Event-driven automation has progressed from basic event matching to sophisticated correlation, and the organization is ready to trust automated systems to handle the majority of operational incidents autonomously while maintaining appropriate human oversight for complex scenarios.

Establish self-healing operations where auto-remediation handles common incident patterns with documented success rates exceeding eighty percent, escalation rules trigger human intervention for complex or novel events, and post-incident reports are generated automatically.

Configure auto-remediation workflows for well-understood incident patterns with verification steps confirming successful resolution, implement escalation rules that route complex events to on-call engineers with full event context, enable automated post-incident reporting generating timeline reconstructions from event processing logs, and ensure in-flight event persistence prevents event loss during controller maintenance.

Self-healing infrastructure operations reduce MTTR from hours to seconds for common incident patterns, freeing operations teams from routine firefighting to focus on strategic reliability improvements, while escalation rules and post-incident reporting maintain organizational visibility and continuous improvement.

activities.name: Govern Decision Environment Lifecycle
activities.description: Establish governed catalog of approved decision environments with security scanning.

narratives.name: Governing Decision Environment Images Through Security and Lifecycle Policies
narratives.description: How to establish governed catalogs with security validation and lifecycle management.

narrativeContexts.context: Organizations operating multiple custom decision environments across different event processing domains need consistent security validation, lifecycle management, and change control for these container images.

Without governance, decision environments proliferate without security scanning, accumulate unpatched dependencies, and lack clear ownership or lifecycle policies, creating operational risk in the event processing infrastructure.

Establish a governed catalog of approved decision environments with automated security scanning, usage analytics, lifecycle policies documenting support timelines, automated rebuild pipelines for dependency updates, and approval workflows before new DEs enter the production catalog.
